title: How Gemini Deep Research turns one question into a report
subtitle: A planner agent browses the web for minutes, plans around partial answers, and writes a cited report you can question.
hook: Every page it read stays in context for follow-ups, even the ones the final report never cites.

nodes.label: You
nodes.detail: You bring a research question that a chatbot would answer with a blueprint, like which nuclear reactor startups matter and who supplies them.
nodes.tradeoff: Most Gemini queries are quick asks like the weather, so the product has to signal that this one will take minutes.

nodes.label: Research plan
nodes.detail: Gemini first drafts a research plan and shows it as a card you can edit before pressing start, the way a good analyst shows their approach.
nodes.tradeoff: The card doubles as the cue that this is not a normal chat turn and something long is about to happen.

nodes.label: Planner agent
nodes.detail: Splits the question into facets, decides which can run in parallel and which must wait, and replans after each finding based on what is still missing.
nodes.tradeoff: It always holds partial information, so it must ground on what it found before choosing the next step.

nodes.label: Async job state
nodes.detail: Runs the task in the background for minutes, keeps its state, and notifies you on any device when it is done.
nodes.tradeoff: With many LLM and service calls, something will fail; state management lets it recover instead of dropping the whole task.

nodes.label: Search and browse
nodes.detail: Searches and opens pages, while the UI shows each site it visits in real time. Facts are often split across sources and the same entity appears under different names.
nodes.tradeoff: The web is fragmented and every site lays things out differently, so browsing has to be robust, not a simple scrape.

nodes.label: Research notes
nodes.detail: Keeps recent tasks in full in the long context window, and moves selected research notes from older tasks into a retrieval store the model can still reach.
nodes.tradeoff: Even with long-context models, follow-up questions keep adding pressure, and each memory design has its own trade-offs.

nodes.label: Cited report
nodes.detail: A report thousands of words long, pinned like an artifact so you can ask questions, add sections or change style beside it, and export to Google Docs with citations.
nodes.tradeoff: It lists every source read and every source used; unused ones still stay in context for follow-ups.

flow.text: Asks about the latest breakthroughs in small nuclear reactors.
Gemini shows an editable research plan; you press start.
Picks which facets to research in parallel and which in sequence.
Searches and reads sites, shown live while you wait.
Spots what is still missing and plans the next searches.
Writes a long cited report and notifies you when done.

takeaways.text: Trade inference time for depth: let the model browse as long as it needs, within five minutes.
Long tasks need durable state, so one failed call does not drop the whole research job.
Planning means grounding on partial results, then hunting for the missing piece.
